newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh unveils $2.97 billion annual plan.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh unveils $2.97 billion annual plan.

text.p: Bangladesh on Thursday unveiled a 1997/98 (July-June) Annual Development Plan envisaging total spending of 128 billion taka ($2.9 billion), with emphasis on easing poverty.
The ADP, announced in parliament by Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria while presenting the national budget for the new fiscal year, was 9.4 percent higher than the 1996/97 plan.
The minister said 47 percent of the new ADP fundings would come from internal resources and 53 percent from foreign aid.
Bangladesh receives about $1.8 billion annually from the international donors to finance ADP and imports.

The minister said over half of Bangladesh's 120 million people still lived under the poverty line. He said alleviation of poverty, establishment of social justice and overall improvement in the standard of living are among top priorities.
The 1997/98 ADP aimed to raise growth of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to six percent from the current 5.7 percent, the finance minister said.
"The actual growth has exceeded our target. The target was 5.5 percent (in 1996/97) against the previous year's 4.7 percent."
Acording to Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, Bangladesh recorded its highest GDP in 1973-74 at 9.6 percent.
The crop production in the current year will reach 20.03 million tonnes as against the target of 20.07 million tonnes, an all-time record, agriculture officials said. ($ = 43.55 Bangladesh Taka)
